extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency NEPA practitioners, agency counsel, environmental reviewers, and NEPA coordinators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards for Federal agencies on drafting, structuring, and deciding the appropriate level of NEPA environmental review (CE determinations, EAs/FONSIs, EISs), and on agency procedures to improve concision, accessibility, and efficiency in NEPA processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise and informative environmental documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must prepare environmental documents that are analytical, concise, and informative and can be easily read and understood by decision makers and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ retitles §1500.4 to emphasize concise and informative documents; explains that concision promotes informed and efficient decision making and meaningful public participation and transparency. CEQ adds "e.g.," throughout §1500.4 to show cross-references are non-exclusive examples of strategies for preparing concise and informative documents; declines to add qualifiers like "for example" or "as appropriate" to the introductory paragraph because "e.g.," is used where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer focused analysis on important issues (use 'important' for issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the term 'important' (not 'significant') to modify 'issues'; concentrate analytical effort on issues truly significant to the action rather than amassing needless detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ replaces 'significant' with 'important' in paragraph (f) to reserve 'significant' for effects; agencies should ensure level of analysis is commensurate with the importance of the effect and concentrate on issues truly significant to the action (consistent with longstanding 1978 approach).

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefly discuss unimportant issues / de-emphasize background material
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should briefly discuss issues that are unimportant and reduce emphasis on background material in environmental documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ adds cross-reference language (with 'e.g.,') to indicate these are non-exclusive ways agencies can briefly discuss unimportant issues and reduce background emphasis; expands references from EISs to all environmental documents where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write in plain language
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental documents should be written in plain language to be easily read and understood by decisionmakers and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ adds 'e.g.,' to show examples of how to write in plain language; plain-language drafting is presented as a mechanism for making documents concise and informative and promoting public participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use errata sheets only for minor changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should use errata sheets for final EISs only when changes between draft and final EIS are minor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ revises paragraph (l) to move the clause 'when changes are minor' to the beginning of the paragraph to clarify that errata sheets are limited to minor changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint preparation of documents by mutual consent (no Tribal coercion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may eliminate duplication by preparing environmental documents jointly with relevant State, Tribal, and local agencies, but joint preparation requires mutual consent and should not be interpreted to compel Tribes to coordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ clarifies paragraph (m) refers agencies to §1506.2 and that joint environmental documents are by mutual consent; rejects interpretation that paragraph (m) obligates Tribes to coordinate with Federal agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary repetition and limit discussion to reasonably foreseeable effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental documents should minimize unnecessary repetition in describing and assessing alternatives and limit discussion of effects to those that are reasonably foreseeable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters asked to add explicit strategies; CEQ declines because existing listed provisions already direct agencies to minimize repetition and evaluate reasonably foreseeable effects; CEQ retains that these are required practices under the regulations referenced in §1500.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve interagency disagreements expeditiously
rubrics_metrics.description: Interagency disagreements should be resolved promptly to improve the efficiency of the NEPA review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although CEQ declined to add more paragraphs to §1500.4, commenters' recommendations to resolve disagreements expeditiously are covered by referenced provisions; later sections (e.g., §1501.1(c)) restore direction regarding expeditious resolution of interagency disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficient process: improve efficiency, not merely reduce delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should make NEPA review processes broadly efficient—emphasizing both timeliness and the effectiveness/quality of work—rather than focusing only on reducing delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ retitles §1500.5 from 'Reducing delay' to 'Efficient process' and revises introductory text accordingly; explains that efficiency includes effectiveness and quality and that unanticipated events may justify different approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish categorical exclusions thoughtfully (change 'using' to 'establishing')
rubrics_metrics.description: Language regarding CEs should address the establishment/development of categorical exclusions, not merely their application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ revises §1500.5(a) to change 'using' to 'establishing' and adds a cross-reference to §1507.3(c)(8) because the provision addresses development of CEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include EAs in references to environmental documents and apply mechanisms across document types
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms to improve efficiency (previously focused on EISs) should apply to all environmental documents, including EAs, so agencies may use similar approaches early in the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ adds EAs to paragraph (a) and expands paragraph (h) from EISs to environmental documents; emphasizes preparing environmental documents early regardless of NEPA review level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use active voice and clear terminology ('deadlines' and 'important issues that require detailed analysis')
rubrics_metrics.description: Drafting and regulatory language should be phrased in active voice and use consistent terminology—e.g., replace 'real issues' with 'important issues that required detailed analysis' and 'time limits' with 'deadlines'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ proposed and adopted these wording changes in §1500.5 to align with §1502.4 and §1501.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency cooperation during document preparation (involve affected agencies early)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead agencies should cooperate with and involve affected Federal, State, Tribal, and local agencies during the preparation of an EA or EIS (and in determinations about CE/EA/EIS), not wait to submit comments on completed documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ revises paragraph (d) to add 'including with affected Federal, State, Tribal, and local agencies' and to add 'request or' before 'submit comments' to highlight the importance of both lead and cooperating agencies requesting or submitting comments and being involved early in determinations about the appropriate level of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency independent responsibility to ensure NEPA compliance and harmonize with other authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies have an independent responsibility to ensure compliance with NEPA and a duty to harmonize NEPA with their other statutory requirements and authorities to the maximum extent possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ revises §1500.6 to emphasize agencies must review and revise procedures to ensure compliance with NEPA and the CEQ regulations and to harmonize NEPA with other statutes wherever possible. CEQ removed language that potentially suggested agencies had no freestanding requirement to comply with NEPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: "To the fullest extent possible": compliance unless exempted or impossible
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'to the fullest extent possible' means each agency must comply with NEPA unless an activity, decision, or action is exempted from NEPA by law or compliance with NEPA is impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ replaces 'that section' with 'the Act' for consistency with statute; declines to change 'impossible' to 'impracticable' and explains 'impossible' is used consistent with case law—only clear, unavoidable statutory conflicts excuse compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify scope of agency discretion when conflicts with other law exist
rubrics_metrics.description: When a clear and fundamental conflict with another provision of Federal law exists, agencies are not required to prepare an environmental document; agencies should not be expected to make additional statutory-interpretation-based determinations in those circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ adds the word 'Federal' to clarify that State, Tribal, or local laws cannot override NEPA and cites section 106(a) of NEPA (42 U.S.C. 4336(a)) as the authority that an agency is not required to prepare an environmental document in such circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate NEPA early in agency planning and emphasize early engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: NEPA should be integrated early into agency planning processes; agencies should engage early and continue engagement throughout the NEPA process to identify and address potential issues and improve outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ restores language from the 1978 regulations in §1501.1 to highlight early integration; adds paragraph (b) emphasizing early engagement and notes the full breadth of engagement is discussed in §1501.9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify scope of proposed action and important environmental issues; tailor analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must identify the scope of the proposed action and the important environmental issues; all issues should be considered but level of analysis should match the importance of the effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ adds paragraph (d) to §1501.1 and declines to require removing unimportant issues from study; instead, agencies may deemphasize issues and allocate analysis commensurate with importance, consistent with 1978 approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedules: develop schedules to promote efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should develop schedules for all environmental reviews and authorizations to promote timeliness and efficient NEPA processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ adds paragraph (e) to §1501.1 referencing §1501.10 and §§1501.7/1501.8 which require schedules and promote interagency coordination regarding schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidated threshold determination process for NEPA applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must determine as a threshold whether NEPA applies to a proposed activity or decision and consolidate the threshold factors and steps determining the appropriate level of NEPA review in §1501.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ moves threshold considerations from §1501.1 into §1501.3 to improve clarity and to align with section 106 of NEPA; the consolidated approach clarifies steps for assessing applicability and appropriate review level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold factors for NEPA applicability: exempted by law
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should consider whether a proposed activity or decision is 'exempted from NEPA by law' as a primary threshold factor in determining NEPA applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ moves and aligns language to require agencies to consider whether actions are exempted from NEPA by law (replacing older phrasing). Such exemptions include specific statutory exemptions recognized by courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold factors for NEPA applicability: clear and fundamental conflict with another Federal law
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should determine whether compliance with NEPA would clearly and fundamentally conflict with the requirements of another provision of Federal law; if so, an agency is not required to prepare an environmental document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ incorporates language from section 106(a)(3) of NEPA into §1501.3(a)(2), adds the word 'Federal' to avoid confusion, and explains agencies need not perform further statutory-interpretation balancing where a clear and fundamental federal statutory conflict exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not expand 'functional equivalence' beyond narrow contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ removes the separate regulatory factor on 'functional equivalence' to avoid suggesting broad new NEPA exemptions; functional equivalence exists only in narrow, judicially recognized contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ strikes the functional equivalence factor from §1501.1(a)(6) because it could be construed to expand exemptions beyond judicially recognized narrow contexts; CEQ treats such cases as 'exempted from NEPA by law' under §1501.3(a)(1) rather than a separate doctrine in the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add factor for statutory provisions that make compliance impossible
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should consider whether statutory provisions applicable to a proposed activity or decision make compliance with NEPA impossible as a threshold factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ proposed and adopts a new factor addressing circumstances where statutory provisions make compliance with NEPA impossible; CEQ ties this to case law and statutory construction and treats 'impossible' as the appropriate standard for excusal.
